rationale: The evidence pack covers docs, plugin mechanics, and community reactions to skill usefulness, but contains no information about release cadence, issue triage, or accepted community pull requests for the anthropics/skills repository. No changelog, GitHub issue/PR activity, or contribution-acceptance evidence is present.

Anthropic ships an official meta-skill (skill-creator) explicitly designed to author and iteratively improve new skills, plus a formal SKILL.md template, a public specification (agentskills.io) defining required frontmatter/description fields, and a runtime probe confirming skills install cleanly as spec-conformant folders usable by third-party tooling. Community evidence corroborates that skills are simple markdown+YAML folders that users create themselves. missing for 10: no independent hands-on report of an agent using skill-creator autonomously end-to-end to produce a new packaged skill (only docs and install probes, not authoring probes).

A recorded real-world probe shows an actual non-interactive, keyless, end-to-end skill install (`npx -y skills add anthropics/skills --skill skill-creator -a claude-code -y --copy`) that fetched the official repo and installed a spec-conformant SKILL.md with no prompts or account needed, confirming headless installability is achievable. However, this relies on third-party npx tooling rather than a documented first-party Anthropic CLI flag for non-interactive `/plugin install` or skill install inside Claude Code itself. Missing for 10: first-party documented non-interactive/headless install command from Anthropic's own CLI, and independent corroboration beyond one recorded probe run.

The Claude Code docs site serves a working llms.txt (HTTP 200 with a documentation index) plus per-page .md variants (e.g. skills.md) explicitly designed for agent consumption, matching the story of pointing an agent at agent-oriented docs. Missing for 10: independent third-party confirmation of llms.txt completeness/coverage beyond the index, and no evidence of llms.txt on the platform.claude.com API docs domain.

Skills like xlsx/docx/pdf processing and the general framing 'analyzing data using your organization's specific workflows' show Claude can generate insights/suggestions from user data files via installed Skills, and this is verified hands-on (skill-creator install works). However, this is a generic extensibility mechanism rather than a dedicated insights feature, and community reports show skills are frequently not invoked reliably (56% non-invocation in Vercel eval, users struggling to get skills triggered), undermining consistent delivery of data-driven insights. Missing for 10: dedicated first-party insights/analytics UI, proactive suggestion generation independent of explicit skill invocation, and evidence that skill-based data analysis reliably triggers without manual prompting.

Skills/plugins let Claude invoke packaged capabilities automatically within a session or via slash-command trigger, but nothing in the evidence describes scheduling, cron-like triggers, or agents running unattended in the background without a live user session — the closest is hooks/agents in plugins, which aren't documented as autonomous background schedulers. missing for 10: evidence of scheduled/triggered background execution, evidence of unattended run completion/notification, and any docs framing skills as an automation/orchestration layer rather than an in-session capability library.

Anthropic's docs claim Claude (the built-in assistant) automatically detects and loads relevant skills to handle delegated tasks, or can be invoked directly via /skill-name (anthropic-skills-docs-2, anthropic-skills-docs-25). However, hands-on/independent evidence concretely contradicts the automatic-delegation claim: Vercel's evaluation found skills were never invoked in 56% of relevant cases with no improvement over baseline, and multiple practitioners report skills are 'hit or miss' or nearly impossible to trigger even when explicitly relevant (anthropic-skills-comm-7, anthropic-skills-comm-8, anthropic-skills-comm-9). Missing for 10: reliable automatic task delegation without manual invocation, independent benchmarks showing consistent trigger accuracy, resolution of the documented invocation-failure reports.

Skills can be invoked programmatically via the Messages API (`container` parameter with skill_id) and managed via the Skills API, which by nature runs headlessly and could be scripted into CI pipelines; the skill-creator tooling also supports non-interactive install/testing via CLI flags like --plugin-dir. However, there is no first-party CI/automation guide, no GitHub Actions example, and no explicit documentation of a 'headless mode' or CI-specific workflow for skills. missing for 10: explicit CI/automation documentation or example, dedicated headless-mode flag/guide, independent evidence of running skills unattended in a pipeline.

Docs show that Claude Code plugins — the packaging mechanism used alongside Skills — can bundle MCP servers together with skills, agents, and hooks (anthropic-skills-docs-6, -7, -21, -35), implying an ai-native user could add an MCP server via the plugin/marketplace system. However, Skills themselves are a separate mechanism (plain SKILL.md instructions), and community commentary explicitly notes skills and MCP are distinct, sometimes competing approaches with skills lacking MCP's tool-calling functionality (anthropic-skills-comm-3, -10). Missing for 10: concrete first-party guide/example of installing an MCP server via a skill or plugin, hands-on confirmation that MCP tools become usable once added this way, and clarity on whether Skills (as opposed to Claude Code plugins broadly) directly expose MCP tool use.

Anthropic Skills is a packaging/format for capabilities (SKILL.md files, plugins, marketplaces) consumed by Claude/Claude Code, not a service or agent that itself exposes an official MCP server endpoint for other agents to connect to. Evidence mentions plugins can *bundle* MCP servers as one of several extension types, but this is about extending Claude Code, not Skills serving as an MCP server itself — the axis is a category mismatch for this product type.

Docs claim Claude will auto-invoke skills 'when relevant' based on natural-language context, in addition to explicit `/skill-name` commands (anthropic-skills-docs-2, -25, -34), which directly supports natural-language operation. However, hands-on community reports concretely contradict reliability of this auto-triggering: Vercel's eval found skills were never invoked in 56% of cases despite being relevant, and multiple users report skills are 'hit or miss' or 'incredibly hard' to get triggered via natural language alone, sometimes requiring explicit prompting to use a named skill (anthropic-skills-comm-7, -8, -9). Missing for 10: independent benchmark showing reliable natural-language triggering, and resolution of the documented invocation-failure reports.

Claude Code is Anthropic's official CLI, and Skills are natively invoked through it via slash commands (`/skill-name`), plugin management (`/plugin marketplace add`, `/plugin install`), and auto-inferred build/run commands (`/run`, `/verify`), all documented in first-party docs and confirmed by a real hands-on install probe. Missing for 10: independent third-party benchmarking specifically of the CLI workflow (community evidence is more about skill-triggering reliability than the CLI itself) and no evidence of CLI-specific edge cases beyond docs/probe.

Anthropic documents a Skills API (upload/manage skills, create endpoint) and shows Skills invoked programmatically via the Messages API `container` parameter (up to 20 skills per request, skill_id/type/version), giving AI-native users a documented public API path distinct from the Claude Code CLI/UI. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on developer corroboration of calling this API, and fuller API reference details (auth, rate limits, error handling) beyond the guide snippets.

Anthropic Skills is a mechanism for packaging instructions/tools for Claude to use, not a credential/access-control system for issuing scoped API keys to agents; nothing in the evidence pack concerns credential scoping or least-privilege API key issuance. This is a category mismatch — the axis belongs to identity/access-management products, not to a skills-packaging framework.

Anthropic provides official SDK/API integration for Skills via the Messages API `container` parameter and Skills API for upload/management, plus documented spec (SKILL.md format, frontmatter, description requirements) that third parties can build against, corroborated by a real runtime probe showing spec-conformant, tooling-installable skills. missing for 10: deeper independent third-party SDK usage examples beyond the official docs, and community evidence is mixed on invocation reliability though that's about triggering not SDK availability.
Anthropic Skills is a mechanism for packaging instructions/tools for Claude to invoke, not an event-driven webhook subscription system; webhooks are a category error for this product type.

Anthropic Skills is a mechanism for packaging agent capabilities (SKILL.md files, plugins), not an API-reference product with an interactive documentation explorer; 'runnable examples in an API reference' is a category mismatch for this product type.

The evidence mentions a Skills API and a specification.md for the SKILL.md file format (agentskills.io), but neither is an OpenAPI or machine-readable API spec for the Skills API itself — no OpenAPI/JSON/YAML spec download is documented anywhere in the pack. The axis applies since Skills exposes an API surface (Messages API container parameter, Skills API endpoints), but no evidence shows a downloadable machine-readable spec for it.

Skills invoked via the Messages API run inside Anthropic's 'code execution environment' (a sandboxed container), and plugin docs mention testing skills locally with the `--plugin-dir` flag before sharing/distribution, which implies some separation from a live/production setup. However, there is no explicit documentation of a dedicated sandbox/staging environment for testing skills against non-production data, no discussion of data isolation guarantees, and no hands-on validation of this specific safety property. Missing for 10: explicit sandbox/staging environment documentation, data-isolation guarantees, and independent confirmation that local/test skill runs cannot touch production data.

The evidence pack documents Skills API usage, optional versioning of skill_id in the container parameter, and plugin marketplace 'version tracking', but there is no documented API versioning scheme or deprecation policy (e.g., version lifecycle, sunset timelines, breaking-change notices) anywhere in the docs.

Anthropic provides an explicit SKILL.md template (with placeholder frontmatter fields like name/description) and a formal spec defining required frontmatter fields, plus a dedicated 'skill-creator' skill whose purpose is to help authors create and iteratively improve new skills without needing to reverse-engineer existing ones; a runtime probe confirms the template/spec-conformant SKILL.md installs and reads back cleanly via third-party tooling. Missing for 10: a first-party step-by-step 'getting started authoring a skill' tutorial narrative and independent developer testimony specifically praising ease of authoring from the template (community commentary instead focuses on invocation reliability, not authoring difficulty).

The repo ships a dedicated skill-creator SKILL.md whose stated purpose is 'creating new skills and iteratively improving them,' including benchmarking skill performance and optimizing descriptions for triggering accuracy, plus a template SKILL.md and packaging guidance (frontmatter, bundled files, plugin manifests) for distribution. Runtime probe confirms it installs cleanly as a real skill via third-party tooling. missing for 10: independent hands-on account of actually using skill-creator to author a new skill end-to-end, and clearer coverage of the 'packaging for distribution via marketplace' step being driven by the meta-skill itself rather than separate plugin docs.

Skills can bundle scripts that process multiple items (e.g., the PDF skill 'merges multiple PDFs', and skills can include arbitrary bash/python scripts for batch tasks), showing the mechanism could support bulk operations, but there is no dedicated bulk-operation feature, no documentation of processing large item sets, and community reports note skills are often not reliably invoked. Missing for 10: explicit bulk/batch processing documentation, evidence of scale (many items processed reliably), and confirmation that triggering works consistently for bulk workflows rather than single tasks.

Anthropic documents that Skills can be configured to auto-invoke when Claude judges them 'relevant' (docs-3, docs-25, docs-34), which is the closest analog to rule-based automatic triggering—there's no true event-driven (e.g., webhook/schedule/file-change) rule engine evidenced, only semantic-relevance triggering by the model itself. Hands-on community reports directly contradict reliable automatic triggering: Vercel found skills were never invoked in 56% of eval cases despite being available, and multiple users report auto-invocation is 'hit or miss' even with explicit YAML triggers, sometimes requiring manual instruction to use them. Missing for 10: genuine event-based rule definitions (not just semantic relevance), reliable automatic firing without manual prompting, and evidence of true trigger-on-event automation outside the coding-agent context.

The evidence pack describes Skills as on-demand or auto-triggered instruction modules invoked by Claude during a task (via /skill-name, semantic triggering, or API container calls), but nothing describes a scheduler, cron-like trigger, or persistent recurring job mechanism. Automation-depth for scheduling is a fair ask for an agentic tool, but no evidence shows Skills or Claude Code support recurring/scheduled execution.

Plugin marketplaces provide 'version tracking' and automatic updates, and plugin manifests carry version fields, and the Skills API lets you pin an optional 'version' per skill_id — giving some versioning primitives. But there is no documented review workflow, diff/audit trail, or explicit rollback mechanism for skills/automations; skills are just filesystem folders, implying reliance on external git for true version control rather than a built-in capability.

missing for 10: explicit rollback/revert mechanism, built-in review/approval workflow, audit history or diffing UI, first-party guidance on reverting a skill/plugin to a prior version.

Anthropic provides a 'plugin marketplace' concept (`/plugin marketplace add`, centralized discovery, version tracking) and an official GitHub repo (anthropics/skills) that developers can browse before installing skills/plugins, with runtime evidence confirming skills can be listed and selectively installed from that repo. However, there's no dedicated searchable UI, leaderboard, or ranking system — discovery is limited to browsing a git repo folder structure or adding marketplaces manually. Missing for 10: a true searchable/filterable catalog UI, ratings or popularity leaderboard, and independent evidence of a broader third-party marketplace ecosystem being actively used.

Docs describe how to create, invoke, and bundle skills via SKILL.md files, plugins, and marketplaces, but no evidence documents a command or workflow for listing all installed skills or removing a skill (and its supporting files/frontmatter) cleanly — only a global disableBundledSkills toggle exists, not per-skill uninstall/listing. Missing for 10: a 'list installed skills' command, a documented 'remove/uninstall skill' command, and confirmation that removal leaves no orphaned files or lingering instructions.

Anthropic's docs state plugin marketplaces provide 'version tracking' and 'automatic updates' (docs-8, docs-36), and plugins support 'versioned releases' (docs-7) — this is the documented update path since skills are commonly distributed as plugins. However, no explicit `/plugin update` (or equivalent) command is shown in the evidence, and standalone skills (installed via SKILL.md folders, not plugins) have no documented update mechanism beyond manual reinstall/copy.  Missing for 10: an explicit update command example, and update-path evidence for bare (non-plugin) skills.

Docs and GitHub instructions show skills are just a folder with a SKILL.md file, installable via a single `/plugin marketplace add` + `/plugin install` command or via `npx skills add`, and a recorded hands-on probe confirms a real end-to-end keyless install of a working skill into a scratch project. This directly demonstrates a fast, low-friction path from zero to an installed skill.

missing for 10: an explicit timed quickstart tutorial/video showing the full flow completing in under 5 minutes, and independent third-party confirmation of install speed beyond the single probe.

Skills are plain, git-hosted directories (SKILL.md plus bundled files) that can be browsed on GitHub before installation and are copied locally as readable markdown/scripts afterward — confirmed by docs describing the folder structure and by a real end-to-end probe that fetched and installed a skill-creator skill whose SKILL.md 'read back cleanly' post-install. However, there is no documented first-party command to enumerate/preview a skill's full file listing or contents specifically before running `/plugin install` or adding a skill (no 'skill inspect' or manifest-diff tool), so review relies on manually browsing the source repo rather than a built-in audit feature.

missing for 10: a dedicated pre-install content-listing/audit command, documented guidance for reviewing scripts/instructions before installation, independent confirmation of full post-install file enumeration beyond SKILL.md.

The Skills format is an open, portable spec (agentskills.io) — plain SKILL.md folders with no Anthropic-specific runtime — and a hands-on probe shows a third-party CLI (`npx skills add ... -a claude-code`) installing skills with a harness-selection flag, implying support for targeting different agents. However, all first-party Anthropic docs (code.claude.com, platform.claude.com) only describe installation/use inside Claude Code or the Claude API/container, with no vendor-provided instructions for Codex, Cursor, or other harnesses. Missing for 10: official multi-harness install docs from Anthropic, confirmed working install/run in Codex or Cursor, and per-harness invocation guidance beyond the inferred CLI flag.

Anthropic documents one-line install commands (`/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`, `/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills`) and a real runtime probe confirms `npx -y skills add anthropics/skills --skill skill-creator ... --copy` actually fetches and installs a skill into `.claude/skills/` with a valid SKILL.md, ready for the next session. Missing for 10: independent third-party corroboration beyond the single probe, and explicit confirmation the skill is 'active' (auto-loaded) immediately in the next session rather than just present on disk.

Anthropic's skills are documented as plain folders with a SKILL.md file containing YAML frontmatter and instructions, and the open agentskills.io specification (name, description, directory structure) matches this exact format, with fields like the 1-1024 character description requirement mirrored in Anthropic's own SKILL.md templates. A recorded runtime probe further shows a third-party CLI tool (not Anthropic's) successfully fetching and installing a skill folder from Anthropic's repo with clean frontmatter, demonstrating real cross-tool portability without any Anthropic account. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement from Anthropic committing to spec conformance/versioning, and broader evidence of multiple independent (non-Anthropic) tools consuming the same skill folders.

The Skills API (container parameter in Messages API, Skills API for upload/manage, skill_id references) lets developers create, upload, and invoke skills programmatically, mirroring what's available in Claude.ai/Claude Code UI (docs-10, docs-23, docs-24, docs-39, gh-2). However, plugin marketplaces, slash-command invocation (/skill-name, /run, /verify), and plugin management appear to be CLI/UI-only constructs with no documented API equivalent, and there's no explicit vendor statement confirming full UI/API parity. Missing for 10: explicit parity documentation, API equivalents for plugin marketplace/slash-command features, and independent confirmation that all UI-surfaced skill behaviors are reproducible via API.

Anthropic Skills is a packaging format/feature for Claude and Claude Code, both of which depend on Anthropic's proprietary hosted model API; no evidence anywhere in the pack shows a way to self-host the core Claude model or Claude Code service on your own infrastructure. The probe showing skill files can be installed locally (anthropic-skills-probe-rt-1) only concerns the open SKILL.md format, not self-hosting the underlying AI product itself.

Anthropic's spec and docs require every SKILL.md to include a description of what the skill does and when to use it, plus frontmatter to control whether Claude or the user triggers it (docs-17, docs-44, docs-34, docs-3) — strong documentation of intended activation. But independent hands-on reports directly contradict predictability: Vercel found skills went uninvoked in 56% of eval cases despite being documented and available, and multiple developers report triggering is 'hit or miss' even with proper YAML descriptions, sometimes needing to explicitly force the skill (comm-7, comm-8, comm-9).
